To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of phase space in multi-particle calculations can be done efficiently by using the phase-space slicing method and that the inclusion of one loop corrections can be done in a very efficient way by applying the sector decomposition method.
the numerical evaluation of the phase space of multi-particle processes is feasible and that the inclusion of loop corrections is possible for processes with up to six external particles.
- The integration of phase-space can be performed efficiently by using Monte-Carlo methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of methods to improve the precision of calculations of multi-particle processes, in particular of processes with many external particles, and to reduce the time and effort needed for the calculations.
methods for the numerical evaluation of multi-particle processes in the framework of quantum field theory.
methods and tools for the numerical evaluation of multi-particle matrix elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calculation of multi-particle processes with one-loop corrections is still a challenge.
the calculation of multi-particle processes at the one-loop level is feasible, but that it is a challenging and time-consuming task.
the calculation of the cross-section for the process e ^{+} e ^{-} → 4 leptons at the order α ^{2} is feasible, but not easy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have made a step in the direction of a more efficient implementation of multi-loop calculations.

we have developed new methods for calculations of multi-particle processes at one-loop order, which are applicable for the first time in a realistic context, i.e. for processes with a large number of final-state particles.

we have found a way to calculate the one-loop amplitudes for multi-particle final states in a numerically efficient way, which is also applicable to processes with a high number of external particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computational complexity of multi-particle processes can be significantly reduced, and the precision increased, by using a combination of techniques.
, in spite of the difficulties, multi-particle calculations are feasible.
the integration of phase space is not the bottleneck in the calculation.
